intro: Occlusion augmentation removes a selected spatial region. Clip the requested rectangle to the image and record the region actually changed.
task: Replace the pixels in a half-open rectangle with a fill value and return an erased-position mask.
requirements: image is a matrix. rectangle is [top,left,bottom,right] with integer entries in -64..128; top<=bottom and left<=right. fill is a real scalar.

Clip each coordinate to the corresponding image bounds. Replace rows top:bottom and columns left:right. Return {"image": new matrix, "mask": boolean matrix}. Empty or fully outside rectangles change nothing.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Clip boundaries before constructing the region; negative Python slice indices would mean something different.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Half-open coordinates make erased area equal to height times width after clipping.

explanation: A deterministic erasing primitive lets a separate sampling policy decide location and size. Returning the mask makes the actual intervention observable for tests or paired tasks.
The rectangle can cross image boundaries, so requested area and effective area may differ. Preserving the original input prevents an augmentation from unexpectedly changing another training view.
